title: Network Architecture and Topology
summary: Trace how endpoints, switches, gateways, and uplinks form a network path.
objectives: Identify dependencies and possible alternate paths.
Separate visible connections from assumptions about traffic.

vocab.def: The arrangement and relationships of devices and links in a network.
A connection from a local device or switch toward another network device or segment.
A device or system that sends or receives network traffic.

sections.heading: Read the path
sections.body: A topology diagram is a model. Trace endpoint to switch, switch to uplink, and uplink to gateway while noting which devices depend on each link.

sections.heading: Look for dependencies
sections.body: If several endpoints share one switch or uplink, that component is a dependency. A second path can reduce the effect of one failed link, but only if it is connected and configured for that purpose.

practice.prompt: A server connects to Switch A, Switch A connects to a gateway, and Switch B has no link to the gateway. Which path should you trace first?
practice.answer: Trace the server to Switch A and then the gateway; Switch B is not part of that visible path.

quiz.question: What does a topology diagram help you determine?
options: Which devices and links form a possible path
The private password for every device
The exact cause of every outage
Whether a cable is safe to touch while energized
quiz.answer: Which devices and links form a possible path

lab.objective: Trace a synthetic network path and identify dependencies.

criteria: Identifies major devices and relevant path

reflectionPrompt: Which shared link would affect the most endpoints, and what evidence supports that idea?
